title: Vertex Systems - platform security & hosting options intake
summary: Introductory security intake for eval of hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary concerns: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence, SSO/SAML integration and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and org-level separation, audit logs retention and format, customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM options, and data residency/retention policy. Agreed to run a focused POC for a small internal app and provide SOC2 docs and deployment diagrams.
topics: Hosting modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
action_items: Maya Chen: send SOC2 and ISO attestation PDFs + security one-pager by 2026-01-26
Rafael Ortiz: share deployment diagram for Private VPC option and sample network ACLs by 2026-01-29
Tom Reynolds: provide list of required audit fields (log schema) and retention threshold by 2026-01-28
Vertex (Priya): confirm pilot app traffic profile and preferred region by 2026-01-30
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 and ISO artifacts + security checklist
Schedule SE-led deep dive / demo of Dedicated capacity (30-45 mins)
Provision trial keys for pilot and agree on metrics (latency/cost)
Vertex to circulate internal approvals for network allowlist for POC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-23 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Rafael, Lena (Redwood); Priya, Tom, Ellen, Samir (Vertex)

Summary (auto): initial security posture intake; mix of compliance and infra questions; plan pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh this is Maya from Redwood, AE. Rafael and Lena are with me from the SE team. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Priya Singh: good thanks, uh excited to get into this. quick note we run a couple of inference endpoints for our internal ops and want to understand where Redwood fits especially around compliance and keys.
[00:17] Rafael Ortiz: cool, thanks Priya. quick agenda — SOC2/ISO attestation, identity integration (SSO/SAML + SCIM), RBAC model, audit logs and retention, and options for hosted / dedicated / private deployments. sounds about right?
[00:28] Tom Reynolds: yep that's right. we are particularly worried about key management and whether we can bring our own keys — KMS or even an HSM.
[00:36] Lena Park: absolutely. we support customer-managed keys, and for Private we can integrate with a customer's KMS or HSM. for Hosted there's a managed KMS option with customer key wrapping — i may mis-say some terms in the transcript but we'll include docs.
[00:47] Ellen Park: when you say "hosted managed KMS with key wrapping" — does Redwood ever have access to the plaintext model inputs or keys?
[00:55] Rafael Ortiz: good question. short answer: no access to customer-managed keys' plaintext; keys are used to wrap data in the storage layer. for hosted managed keys our service handles envelope encryption but we don't store customer key material. for private deployments customer keys remain in their KMS/HSM.
[01:12] Samir Patel: and rotation? we require rotation every 90 days, ideally automated via your integration with our cloud KMS.
[01:19] Maya Chen: yep rotation is supported; we can trigger rewraps and have documented key rotation procedures. we'll share the runbook.
[01:26] Tom Reynolds: on audit logs — what fields do you capture? we need user identifier, request id, model version, input hash, token counts, response status, and geo-region. retention needs to be at least 7 years for some lines of business.
[01:43] Rafael Ortiz: today we capture request id, timestamp, model id/version, approximate token counters, latency, and error codes. inputs are stored if retention policy enabled; we can emit hashed inputs if you prefer. 7 years is long — we usually keep audit logs for 12 months by default but can extend with enterprise retention plans.
[02:03] Priya Singh: that 12 months default won't fly for some compliance teams. we need options for immutable logs stored in our S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules.
[02:13] Lena Park: that's doable in Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we can push logs to your customer's S3 or to your SIEM via secure forwarder — there are a couple of patterns. we'll attach the design doc.
[02:23] Ellen Park: SOC2 and ISO evidence — can you share the attestation and scope? what trust services you cover for SOC2?
[02:31] Maya Chen: yes — we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. note: for Hosted some controls are shared responsibility, the report shows control boundaries. we'll highlight the pieces that map to your audit.
[02:44] Tom Reynolds: sometimes the PDF reports redact customer data — that's fine. we also want the control matrix mapping to our own policies.
[02:51] Maya Chen: understood, we'll include a controls mapping spreadsheet.
[02:55] [03:00] (crosstalk) Priya: can you also explain how SSO integration works? we run Okta and use SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
[03:08] Rafael Ortiz: Okta + SAML is supported. we provide SAML metadata for Redwood console SSO and SCIM endpoints for user provisioning. role sync is done via SCIM groups and mapped to Redwood RBAC roles. sometimes SCIM attribute mapping needs a tiny bit of glue but we've done it for many customers.
[03:26] Samir Patel: roles — are they org-level? we want separation across environments (prod/stage) and different teams.
[03:33] Lena Park: RBAC is hierarchical: org -> workspace -> route. you can map SCIM groups to org-level roles and we also support fine-grained permissions for model operations, billing views, and keys.
[03:46] Tom Reynolds: can we get audit trails for role changes? like who granted admin to someone, timestamp, IP?
[03:53] Rafael Ortiz: yes, admin actions and role changes are logged with actor id and timestamp. IP is included when possible — depends on where the request originated (e.g., console vs API).
[04:04] Priya Singh: about deployment: our security team is leaning towards Dedicated or Private because of data residency and network controls. what's the main operational difference?
[04:14] Maya Chen: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for your tenant — you get predictable throughput, dedicated GPU pools, and VPC peering for private networking. Private is where we ship a private control plane and optionally an on-prem package into your environment — you manage networking and keys fully. Dedicated still has some centralized control plane elements unless you opt for Private.
[04:36] Ellen Park: how is fallback handled if Dedicated capacity spikes? do you spill to Hosted?
[04:41] Rafael Ortiz: there's a policy-driven fallback. customers can opt in or out of spilling to Hosted. for regulated customers, we can set strict no-spill policies.
[04:51] Tom Reynolds: latency requirements — we need p95 under 150ms for small prompts in our app. can you meet that on Dedicated?
[04:58] Lena Park: depends on model size and batch config. for small sequence lengths on optimized kernels we can get p95 < 150ms on Dedicated with smaller models or quantized variants. we'll need to benchmark with your traffic profile.
[05:12] Priya Singh: ok the pilot: we want to run a POC for one internal ticket summarization microservice — low QPS (5-10 rps) but strict P95 SLOs and 7-year retention of logs. what's minimal scope?
[05:23] Maya Chen: minimal pilot: provide sample traffic, we'll run it on a Dedicated pool and enable extended audit retention to your S3. we'll timebox it for 4 weeks and run latency/cost analysis.
[05:33] Samir Patel: for the S3 logs, do you write encrypted files on our bucket or do you push events to our SIEM?
[05:39] Rafael Ortiz: both options exist. we can write compressed NDJSON to your S3 with SSE-KMS using your key, or stream events to your SIEM via secure connector.
[05:50] Tom Reynolds: what's the SLA around key material for HSM — can you integrate with our on-prem HSM via VPN?
[05:58] Lena Park: Private deployment supports direct integration; for Dedicated we typically integrate with cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) or bring-your-own-key via KMS APIs. on-prem HSM over VPN is possible in Private mode.
[06:10] Priya Singh: about data residency — we need data to be processed in EU region for EU customers, is region pinning available?
[06:17] Maya Chen: yes region pinning is supported; routing policy can keep requests in a specific region. Dedicated pools are region-specific; Private is whatever you deploy into.
[06:26] Ellen Park: any third-party sub processors we should know about?
[06:30] Maya Chen: our list of subprocessors is in the security one-pager; major cloud providers for infra and a few analytics providers. we'll send the latest list and notify you of changes per contract.
[06:40] Tom Reynolds: curious about log immutability — can logs be write-once for compliance?
[06:44] Rafael Ortiz: with S3 Object Lock + governance mode you can get WORM-like immutability. for Hosted we can push to your bucket with the proper retention settings.
[06:53] Priya Singh: anything else on encryption at rest? we want end-to-end — at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys, in transit TLS 1.2+ and ideally mTLS for internal service-to-service.
[07:02] Lena Park: agreed. TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. service-to-service uses mTLS in Dedicated/Private networks. at-rest encryption uses envelope encryption and your KMS when configured.
[07:12] (pause)
[07:18] Maya Chen: quick pause — Rafael and I will follow up with docs. questions from our side: who's going to be the technical owner on your side for the pilot?
[07:25] Priya Singh: Tom will own the technical setup; Samir will coordinate networking.
[07:29] Maya Chen: great. Rafael, do you want to walk through a quick checklist for the pilot?
[07:33] Rafael Ortiz: sure. checklist: 1) confirm pilot traffic and region 2) provide allowlist IPs for Dedicated VPC 3) agree on log schema and retention 4) provide Okta SAML & SCIM details for user provisioning if you want console access 5) determine KMS approach (BYOK or managed) 6) sign limited POC agreement.
[07:54] Tom Reynolds: for the log schema i'll send a doc with the fields we need. also need to verify that input hashing is deterministic so we can reconcile events.
[08:03] Lena Park: hashing is deterministic given the same normalization; we'll include the hashing algorithm and salt approach in docs.
[08:11] Priya Singh: on the POC agreement — we need NDA+data processing addendum.
[08:16] Maya Chen: we'll attach our DPA and the standard POC terms. if you need any special clauses we'll loop legal.
[08:23] Ellen Park: any concerns about vendor lock-in? some teams worry about switching later.
[08:27] Rafael Ortiz: we provide export tools for model configs, prompts, and cached artifacts. for Dedicated/Private you own the infra. our SDKs are standard REST/JSON so migration is straightforward. we'll share a migration playbook.
[08:41] Samir Patel: cost estimate? rough idea for Dedicated baseline for our QPS?
[08:46] Maya Chen: we'll follow up with a pricing sheet and a cost model based on your traffic. initial estimate will include reserved capacity plus network egress.
[08:54] Priya Singh: ok let's recap — Redwood sends SOC2/ISO, controls mapping, SCIM+SAML setup docs, deployment diagram for Private, sample log schema, and pricing for a 4-week Dedicated pilot. Vertex will send traffic profile, log field list, and confirm region.
[09:12] Maya Chen: exactly. Rafael, anything to add?
[09:15] Rafael Ortiz: i'll add a note that for the pilot we'll do basic perf benchmarks and a follow-up meeting week 2 of the pilot to review metrics.
[09:24] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. one nit — when you send the SOC2 please include dates of coverage so our audit team can verify.
[09:31] Maya Chen: will do.
[09:34] [09:40] (wrap up)
[09:43] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll send materials by end of week and propose times for the SE deep dive.
[09:49] Priya Singh: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:51] Ellen Park: thanks all.
[09:54] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS/K-M-S transcribed as KMS or keys), and some timestamps approximate. Links mentioned: security one-pager (link shared in follow-up), controls spreadsheet (to be shared), deployment diagram (to be shared), pilot pricing spreadsheet (to be shared).
